requirements.quote: To enable 0-RTT, endpoints store the values of the server transport parameters with any session tickets it receives on the connection.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint stores a session ticket for later use in enabling 0-RTT.
requirements.required_behavior: Store the server transport-parameter values with the session ticket.
requirements.why_checkable: Ticket persistence can be inspected to verify that the associated server transport-parameter values are retained.

requirements.quote: Endpoints also store any information required by the application protocol or cryptographic handshake; see Section 4.6 of [QUIC-TLS].
requirements.condition: When storing state needed to enable 0-RTT.
requirements.required_behavior: Store the information required by the application protocol or cryptographic handshake.
requirements.why_checkable: The endpoint's persisted 0-RTT state can be checked for all application- and handshake-required information, though the referenced requirements are outside this chunk.

requirements.quote: Remembered transport parameters apply to the new connection until the handshake completes and the client starts sending 1-RTT packets.
requirements.condition: On a new connection using remembered transport parameters, before the handshake completes and the client starts sending 1-RTT packets.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply the remembered transport parameters to the new connection.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can observe which parameter values govern behavior before the transition to post-handshake 1-RTT sending.

requirements.quote: Once the handshake completes, the client uses the transport parameters established in the handshake.
requirements.condition: Once the handshake completes.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the transport parameters established in the handshake.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Continue using remembered transport parameters for behavior governed by the completed handshake.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can complete the handshake with values different from the remembered values and observe which values the client applies.

requirements.quote: The definition of a new transport parameter (Section 7.4.2) MUST specify whether storing the transport parameter for 0-RTT is mandatory, optional, or prohibited.
requirements.condition: When defining a new transport parameter.
requirements.required_behavior: Specify exactly whether storing that parameter for 0-RTT is mandatory, optional, or prohibited.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Leave the parameter's 0-RTT storage status unspecified or specify a status outside those three categories.
requirements.why_checkable: A transport-parameter definition can be inspected for one of the three required storage classifications.

requirements.quote: A client need not store a transport parameter it cannot process.
requirements.condition: When the client cannot process a transport parameter.
requirements.why_checkable: The sentence grants permission but does not impose a required, forbidden, or error behavior on an implementation.

requirements.quote: A client MUST NOT use remembered values for the following parameters: ack_delay_exponent, max_ack_delay, initial_source_connection_id, original_destination_connection_id, preferred_address, retry_source_connection_id, and stateless_reset_token.
requirements.condition: When a client establishes a new connection using remembered transport state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use remembered values of ack_delay_exponent, max_ack_delay, initial_source_connection_id, original_destination_connection_id, preferred_address, retry_source_connection_id, or stateless_reset_token.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can preload distinct remembered values for each named parameter and verify that none governs the new connection.

requirements.quote: The client MUST use the server's new values in the handshake instead; if the server does not provide new values, the default values are used.
requirements.condition: For ack_delay_exponent, max_ack_delay, initial_source_connection_id, original_destination_connection_id, preferred_address, retry_source_connection_id, and stateless_reset_token when the server supplies new values in the handshake.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the server's new handshake values.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Substitute remembered values for the server's new handshake values.
requirements.why_checkable: The server can advertise values differing from stored values and the client's effective values can be observed.

requirements.quote: The client MUST use the server's new values in the handshake instead; if the server does not provide new values, the default values are used.
requirements.condition: For the listed non-remembered parameters when the server does not provide new values.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use remembered values in place of defaults.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can omit the parameters from the handshake and verify that their defined defaults, rather than stored values, take effect.

requirements.quote: A client that attempts to send 0-RTT data MUST remember all other transport parameters used by the server that it is able to process.
requirements.condition: When a client attempts to send 0-RTT data and is able to process a server transport parameter other than the parameters excluded in lines 2061-2064.
requirements.required_behavior: Remember every such transport parameter used by the server.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Attempt to send 0-RTT while omitting a processable, non-excluded server transport parameter from remembered state.
requirements.why_checkable: The client's saved state can be compared with all processable, non-excluded parameters used by the server.

requirements.quote: The server can remember these transport parameters or can store an integrity-protected copy of the values in the ticket and recover the information when accepting 0-RTT data.
requirements.condition: When a server retains transport-parameter values needed to evaluate later 0-RTT acceptance.
requirements.required_behavior: Either remember the values directly, or place an integrity-protected copy in the ticket and recover it when accepting 0-RTT data.
requirements.why_checkable: Server state and ticket handling can be inspected to determine whether one of the described retention mechanisms is used, but the sentence is permissive rather than a complete requirement.

requirements.quote: If 0-RTT data is accepted by the server, the server MUST NOT reduce any limits or alter any values that might be violated by the client with its 0-RTT data.
requirements.condition: When the server accepts 0-RTT data.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reduce a limit or alter a value in a way that the client's 0-RTT data might violate.
requirements.why_checkable: Recorded 0-RTT behavior can be checked against newly selected limits and values to determine whether acceptance makes that behavior invalid.

requirements.quote: In particular, a server that accepts 0-RTT data MUST NOT set values for the following parameters (Section 18.2) that are smaller than the remembered values of the parameters. * active_connection_id_limit * initial_max_data * initial_max_stream_data_bidi_local * initial_max_stream_data_bidi_remote * initial_max_stream_data_uni * initial_max_streams_bidi * initial_max_streams_uni
requirements.condition: When the server accepts 0-RTT data and has remembered values for the listed parameters.
requirements.required_behavior: Set active_connection_id_limit, initial_max_data, initial_max_stream_data_bidi_local, initial_max_stream_data_bidi_remote, initial_max_stream_data_uni, initial_max_streams_bidi, and initial_max_streams_uni to values at least as large as their respective remembered values.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Set any listed parameter below its remembered value.
requirements.why_checkable: Each newly advertised value can be numerically compared with its corresponding remembered value.

requirements.quote: The applicable subset of transport parameters that permit the sending of application data SHOULD be set to non-zero values for 0-RTT.
requirements.condition: When configuring transport parameters to permit application data to be sent in 0-RTT.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the applicable application-data-enabling transport parameters to non-zero values.
requirements.why_checkable: The effective 0-RTT parameter values can be checked for zero values.

requirements.quote: This includes initial_max_data and either (1) initial_max_streams_bidi and initial_max_stream_data_bidi_remote or (2) initial_max_streams_uni and initial_max_stream_data_uni.
requirements.condition: When configuring a non-zero parameter subset that enables application data in 0-RTT.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a non-zero initial_max_data value and provide either non-zero initial_max_streams_bidi plus initial_max_stream_data_bidi_remote, or non-zero initial_max_streams_uni plus initial_max_stream_data_uni.
requirements.why_checkable: The advertised values can be evaluated as the stated Boolean combination of non-zero parameters.

requirements.quote: Once the handshake completes, the client updates the flow control limits on all sending streams using the updated values of initial_max_stream_data_bidi_remote and initial_max_stream_data_uni.
requirements.condition: Once the handshake completes and updated initial_max_stream_data_bidi_remote or initial_max_stream_data_uni values are available.
requirements.required_behavior: Update the flow-control limits on all sending streams using the applicable updated values.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Leave a sending stream governed by the obsolete remembered stream flow-control limit after handshake completion.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can establish streams before completion, advertise larger values, complete the handshake, and inspect every sending stream's limit.

requirements.quote: A server MAY store and recover the previously sent values of the max_idle_timeout, max_udp_payload_size, and disable_active_migration parameters and reject 0-RTT if it selects smaller values.
requirements.condition: When a server selects max_idle_timeout, max_udp_payload_size, or disable_active_migration values smaller than values it previously sent.
requirements.required_behavior: The server is permitted to recover the previous values and reject 0-RTT.
requirements.error_behavior: Reject 0-RTT based on selecting smaller values for these parameters.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can restore larger prior values, select smaller current values, and verify that rejection is an allowed outcome rather than a mandatory one.

requirements.quote: A server MUST reject 0-RTT data if the restored values for transport parameters cannot be supported.
requirements.condition: When restored transport-parameter values cannot be supported by the server.
requirements.why_checkable: A server can be presented with a ticket containing unsupported restored values and its accept/reject decision observed.

requirements.quote: When sending frames in 0-RTT packets, a client MUST only use remembered transport parameters
requirements.condition: When a client sends frames in 0-RTT packets.
requirements.required_behavior: Use only remembered transport-parameter values to govern those frames.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Govern 0-RTT frames using any non-remembered transport-parameter values.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can make remembered and newly learned values differ and observe the values respected by emitted 0-RTT frames.

requirements.quote: it MUST NOT use updated values that it learns from the server's updated transport parameters or from frames received in 1-RTT packets.
requirements.condition: When a client has learned updated values from the server's updated transport parameters or from frames received in 1-RTT packets and is sending 0-RTT packets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use those updated values for frames sent in 0-RTT packets.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can deliver larger updated values through both sources and verify that subsequent 0-RTT output does not use them.

requirements.quote: Updated values of transport parameters from the handshake apply only to 1-RTT packets.
requirements.condition: When updated transport-parameter values are learned from the handshake.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply those updated values only to 1-RTT packets.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet-space-specific behavior can be tested using distinct remembered and handshake-updated values.

requirements.quote: flow control limits from remembered transport parameters apply to all 0-RTT packets even if those values are increased by the handshake or by frames sent in 1-RTT packets.
requirements.condition: When handshake transport parameters or frames sent in 1-RTT packets increase flow-control limits while the client can still send 0-RTT packets.
requirements.required_behavior: Continue applying the remembered flow-control limits to every 0-RTT packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use the increased flow-control limits for any 0-RTT packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can raise the limit after 0-RTT begins and verify that every later 0-RTT packet remains within the remembered limit.

requirements.quote: A server MAY treat the use of updated transport parameters in 0-RTT as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.condition: When a client uses updated transport parameters in 0-RTT.
requirements.error_behavior: The server is permitted to treat the behavior as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can send 0-RTT that relies on an updated value and verify that closing the connection with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION is an allowed response.
